title: Playing stride piano behind Jimmy Rushing in The Learning Tree
summary: A party performance led Gordon Parks to cast him as unseen piano player behind Rushing; the planned gag was cut.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: You were telling me that you were in Gordon's first picture, "The Learning Tree," and you told me how Gordon happened to pick you for that part. Tell me on tape.

Well, this is funny. This is at a party with John Levy and his wife, Gail Fisher at that time. And my wife and everybody, we were all just having a good time, so I sat down and started playing some tongue in cheek piano, stride, not realizing that it was going to become that important, and Gordon possibly had put these things in the back of his mind, and before I knew it I was playing stride piano in the
picture behind the great Jimmy Rushing (RUSHING). And we had -- you know, how they used to wear those straw hats, sailor straw hats, striped shirts with the band around the elbows.
Uh-huh.
Because Rush was -- he was five by five, so consequently he needed more mileage than I did on the dressing department.
(Laughter)
Yeah, we used to sit out and talk and we'd eat lunch, and it came off quite well, you know?
Yeah, I remember the scene, but I don't remember knowing that that was you on piano.
Well, what it was, they shot me from behind, and I was sitting -- Jimmy had like little half pints of tea in his -- it looked like whiskey.
Uh-huh.

And he's telling, in this particular joint that we're supposed to be working in -- and I'm sitting at the piano, an old upright, and it's a flashback. And there was no way for you to know it was me, because you never saw my face.
Uh-huh. I see.
Oh, I have a funny little joke to tell you about that. There was a girl there in the beginning scene, very attractive, still attractive today. I was supposed to
have a line where I would -- as she passed by the piano, I was supposed to pat her on the backside.
Uh-huh.
So I really wound up practicing this thing. I would go to John Levy's office with his secretaries and practice it. Up to the last minute. Gordon changed the script.
Why?

Well, I don't know. He just thought of something else, that's all. Well, we had a lot of people involved in the thing. William Conrad -- oh. They were on the set every day. There was several, you know, heavyweights, I guess. But they would change this, change that, as the movies go. I just wanted that lady to pass by the piano.
(Laughter)

And so I said, 'Gordon, why did you strike me out?' He looked at me and laughed and walked away, you know. But I really enjoyed it. It was another milestone on my behalf. Not knowing that I was going to be there at all. It started out with a joke --
That's interesting.
-- at a party.
Uh-huh. Doing the right thing at the right time in the right place with the right people.
Not planning it or anything, just sitting
down, doing it, or whatever, you know?
